This is the calorie app you made me. Make visually similar app. 

Make a simple app for tracking workouts. Easy to logg sets and reps and to add  new exercises. Have about 10 of the most popular exercies in the app from start "like barbell bench, squat and deadlift". The app should also have a section to se how much you impove at an excerice with graph.

**Considering Design Elements**

I've been analyzing the request, focusing on the visual style. The provided calorie tracker screenshot is key. I'm taking notes on its clean design, soft shadows, rounded corners, and the use of pastel/gradient accents. "Hey" text hints are also noted. These visual elements will guide the UI/UX design decisions, setting the foundation for the workout tracking app's aesthetic. I'm working to translate these visual cues into UI components.


**Designing Application Functionality**

I'm now fully immersed in the app's core features. It'll allow tracking sets, reps, and exercises, with pre-populated options and progress graphs. React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Recharts, and Lucide React are the tech foundation, with no backend. The "Weekly Average" pill design is central. Next, I'll integrate the chosen visual style.


**Planning App Components**

I'm now outlining key UI components. We'll have a header greeting, a date navigator, and a styled button. "Track" and "Progress" views switch with segmented controls. Data will be structured as `Exercise` and `WorkoutLog` in local storage, with an initial exercise list. I'm focusing on `App.tsx`, `components/Header.tsx`, `DashboardCard.tsx`, and workout logging.


**Developing the App Structure**

I'm now fully immersed in the implementation plan, working through each step. I've broken it down to defining the basic data structures and UI components. My focus is now on the mental drafting of the code, especially how to translate data for Recharts and styling the "Weekly Average" element. The purple gradient is a priority. I'm focusing on utility classes to match the design.


**Integrating Visual Feedback**

I'm now integrating the circular progress indicator concept, but will focus on "Sets Completed" and "Volume" metrics, given the nature of a workout app. I've noted the dark, bold font and the dark "Add" button design. With these visual considerations, I'm now drafting the implementation. I'm focusing on the `index.html` boilerplate, and defining the `Exercise`, `Set`, and `WorkoutSession` types in `types.ts`. I'm also preparing the exercise list. The real work is in `App.tsx`, where I'm setting up state for exercises, logs, and view switching. I'm structuring the layout with a Header, Date Navigator, Summary Card, and Bottom Nav.


**Clarifying Tracker Functionality**

I'm now zeroing in on the core tracking mechanics. The user flow is clear: select an exercise, add sets with weight and reps, then save the data. It's crucial to group these logs efficiently by exercise for the current day. I also have the progress feature in mind, incorporating a dropdown for exercise selection, and a line chart displaying max weight lifted over time. The constraints are straightforward: React 18 with `createRoot`, Tailwind-only styling, and no Gemini API integration for now. Code quality and user experience are my primary focus.


**Organizing App Components**

I'm now diving into the final app structure. I've broken down `App.tsx` into more manageable components for clarity, with a `components/` directory for `Tracker`, `Progress`, `SummaryCard`, and `Navigation`. I'm now setting up the Tailwind styles, specifically the purple gradient, card design, and text colors. I've also noted to handle the "Add Exercise" feature and will add the feature as a simple modal. I'm focusing on the final touches, and using lucide-react, recharts, and date-fns as dependencies.


**Refining Data & Graphs**

I'm now clarifying the data structure and deciding on the progress graph. I'm leaning towards native `Intl` for date formatting, unless the dependency count really explodes.  After re-evaluating, `date-fns` seems safer to use. I'm keeping the data model in mind: `logs` will be an array of objects, each containing an ID, date (ISO string), exercise ID, and an array of sets with weight and reps. For the graph, I'll calculate the "Max Weight" for simplicity. I'm focusing on data manipulation now to prepare the information the graph will present.


**Confirming Final Structure**

I'm solidifying the final app structure with focused components. I've re-evaluated and settled on a seven-file structure, ensuring clarity and avoiding over-complication. I've also done a thorough check to ensure the layout matches the visual reference in terms of elements and general screen flow. The header, date, weekly average, and log/stats toggle all match up, and I can start coding the core now.


**Launching the Codebase**

I'm now fully immersed in coding. The seven-file structure is set, and I'm tackling the boilerplate in `App.tsx`. I'm starting with state management for exercises, logs, and view control. I'm focusing on the `Header` and `DateNavigator` components first, aiming for a clean, modular approach.
